bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your SA Teacher Salary: From Hourly to Annual

If you're a teacher in South Australia, you might be offered an hourly rate or a salary figure and want to see the full picture. Converting between hourly, weekly, fortnightly and annual pay is straightforward, but there are important distinctions between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading and superannuation. This guide explains how to calculate your SA teacher salary across different pay periods, using the standard 38-hour full-time week.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The core calculation is: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, that becomes:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $40.00, your annual gross pay would be $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances or salary sacrifice. It's a simple estimate, not a binding determination of your pay.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Figure

Many teachers are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. Weekly pay is hourly rate × 38. So fortnightly pay = (hourly rate × 38) × 2. Using the same $40.00 rate, weekly pay is $1,520, and fortnightly pay is $3,040.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. For casual employees, the minimum casual rate is $33.05 per hour, which includes a 25% casual loading. However, most teachers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award. An SA teacher salary is typically above the minimum wage, but you should check the specific award that applies to your role. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details on the national rate.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual teacher, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator that adds it separately. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide explains how this works.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at the super guarantee rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). For example, if your annual gross pay is $80,000, your employer would contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on your tax bracket and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help you estimate your net income.

### What About the SA Teacher Salary Average?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time in South Australia as $1,970.20 per week (May 2026). This is an average across all occupations and industries, not a median for the teaching profession. Your SA teacher salary may differ based on your classification, experience and school sector. For specific award rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or the [reference tables](/data) on this site.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Using the Timesheet

If you want to calculate your own figures, the [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember to enter your base rate without casual loading if you use the checkbox.

### Summary

Converting your SA teacher salary from hourly to annual is simple: multiply by 38 and then by 52. But always check whether you are covered by an award or agreement that sets a higher rate than the National Minimum Wage. Super is paid on top, and tax is deducted according to the 2026–27 brackets. Use the tools on this site to get a clearer picture of your pay.
